anti_patterns: Shipping production on default Security Stack: lazy opt-in to LayerZero-admin defaults hands verification choice to a third party; explicitly configure required DVNs per pathway
Single-DVN receive config with no optional threshold: one compromised or buggy verifier can commit arbitrary payload hashes; require at least one independent second verifier
Treating cross-chain delivery as synchronous: blocking source-chain UX on destination finality instead of emitting pending state and reconciling on PacketDelivered
Setting send config but forgetting the receive config on the destination chain: messages verify against defaults or stall because no receive library is authorized for the pathway
Enabling ordered delivery without ExecutorOrderedExecutionOption in send options: the executor attempts unordered execution and the OApp nonce check reverts every message
Calling endpoint.skip/clear without syncing the OApp receivedNonce mapping: protocol and app nonce state diverge and all subsequent ordered messages revert with invalid nonce

Underfunding executor gas (lzReceive option) or omitting lzCompose gas: destination execution runs out of gas while verification already paid; message sits verified-but-undelivered until manual execution
Registering peers by raw address without per-chain peer checks (peers[srcEid] == origin.sender): any contract on the source chain can spoof messages into _lzReceive
Ignoring source-finality confirmations on high-value lanes: low confirmation counts let reorged burns/mints commit on the destination with no backing transaction
avoid_when: Only one chain is involved (no cross-chain movement at all)
Sub-second or synchronous cross-chain latency is required (delivery waits source finality plus DVN verification plus executor)
Atomic all-or-nothing execution across chains is required (FLP impossibility: no OMP can coordinate atomic commits over an asynchronous network)
The application cannot tolerate dependence on off-chain worker liveness (stalled DVNs or executors freeze delivery even when both chains are healthy)
A single organization controls all chains and trusts its own sequencer (a native bridge or shared sequencer is simpler)
Messages exceed the executor maxMessageSize without chunking strategy (delivery reverts; use batched or referenced payloads)
best_practices: Explicitly configure the Security Stack per pathway (send library, receive library, UlnConfig with confirmations, required and optional DVNs) and never rely on admin defaults in production
Require DVN client diversity: combine verification technologies (e.g. ZK proof plus oracle committee) so one bug class cannot forge a quorum
Scale block confirmations with value at risk: higher confirmations on high-value lanes, lower on low-value fast lanes
Set enforced options (executor gas, value, ordering flag) per destination chain and profile _lzReceive gas on each destination before mainnet
Whitelist peers bilaterally with setPeer on every chain before enabling a lane; verify peer addresses out of band
Plan Security Stack migration with grace periods: authorize the new receive library while in-flight messages on the old version drain, then retire the old library
Monitor PacketSent/PacketVerified/PacketDelivered events per pathway and alert on verification-without-delivery (executor stall) separately from send-without-verification (DVN stall)
Keep manual-execution fallback runbooked (LayerZero Scan or direct lzReceive calls) so executor outages degrade to slow delivery, not frozen funds
Use nilify proactively on suspected compromised-DVN packets and clear/skip only through governed functions that sync app-level nonce state
benefits: No intermediate chain or wrapped-token hop: source Endpoint talks directly to destination Endpoint, so there is no middlechain consensus tax or extra finality delay
Ultra-light on-chain footprint: block headers and proofs are fetched by off-chain workers, not replicated on-chain, keeping verification O(1) per message even on expensive L1s

Per-pathway configurable security: each OApp sets its own UlnConfig (confirmations, required DVNs, optional threshold), trading verification cost against trust per lane instead of accepting monolithic shared security

Immutable Endpoint with append-only MessageLibs: the application-facing interface never changes, and security upgrades add new library versions with grace-period migration rather than forced in-place updates
Permissionless worker markets: anyone can run a DVN or executor, so verification and delivery compete on cost and latency instead of depending on one bridge operator
Lossless exactly-once channel semantics: GUID plus gapless nonces with getInboundNonce accounting guarantee no loss, no duplication, and ordered or unordered delivery per application choice
Unified omnichain application model: the OApp facade (_lzSend/_lzReceive, peers, enforced options) plus OFT/ONFT standards make one contract deployable across EVM, Solana, and Move chains
component_types: Endpoint (Immutable Interface): one contract per chain exposing send/quote/verify/lzReceive, GUID plus nonce channel accounting, PacketSent/PacketVerified/PacketDelivered events
MessageLib Registry: append-only on-chain verification rulesets (e.g. SendULN302/ReceiveULN302) selected per pathway by the OApp Security Stack
UlnConfig (Quorum Policy): per-pathway struct of confirmations, requiredDVNCount, optionalDVNCount, optionalDVNThreshold, and sorted DVN address sets
DVN (Decentralized Verifier Network): off-chain worker plus on-chain contract implementing assignJob/getFee; verifies payload hashes via multisig, ZK proofs, oracle, adapter, or light-client logic
Executor: off-chain delivery worker that calls Endpoint.lzReceive (and lzCompose for composed messages) with caller-specified gas and value
OApp Facade: application base contract wrapping Endpoint calls with _lzSend/_lzReceive, peer registry, fee quoting, and enforced execution options
OFT/ONFT Standards: token templates built on OApp implementing burn/mint (or lock/unlock adapter) debit-and-credit with unified cross-chain supply
Message Options (OptionsBuilder): serialized per-message execution requests (lzReceive gas/value, ordered-execution flag, lzCompose calls) interpreted by workers
context: An application must send arbitrary messages or move assets between heterogeneous blockchains (EVM, Solana, Move) without trusting an intermediate chain, running full light clients on every chain, or accepting one bridge operator's monolithic security. LayerZero structures this as omnichain messaging: an immutable Endpoint on each chain forms a fully connected mesh, off-chain oracles/relayers (V1) or permissionless DVN quorums (V2) attest to source-chain payloads, and independent executors deliver verified messages to destination contracts with lossless exactly-once semantics.
design_principles: Interface-Verification-Execution Separation: immutable Endpoint, replaceable MessageLibs, and permissionless workers evolve independently
Application-Owned Security: each OApp configures its own Security Stack per pathway; no shared global verifier set can be forced on it
Independence as Trust Root: V1 requires oracle and relayer to be non-colluding; V2 generalizes this to required-plus-threshold DVN quorums with client diversity
Intrinsic Over Extrinsic: censorship resistance, replay protection, and exactly-once delivery are enforced immutably on-chain; signature schemes and verifier sets stay swappable
Lossless Exactly-Once Channel: gapless nonces with getInboundNonce accounting make skipped or failed messages explicit rather than silently dropped
Update Isolation: MessageLib upgrades are append-only with grace-period migration so in-flight messages drain on the old version
Fail Explicit: unverified, nilified, or skipped nonces halt or skip delivery visibly instead of executing optimistically

create-lz-oapp CLI and LayerZero Scan indexer
tradeoffs: Trust reduces to worker independence: V1 is broken if the default oracle and relayer collude; V2 is only as strong as the independence and diversity of the configured DVN set
Liveness depends on off-chain workers: stalled or censoring DVNs/executors freeze delivery even when both chains are healthy; manual execution is the only fallback
Latency is finality-bound and asynchronous: source confirmations plus DVN verification plus executor delivery rule out instant or atomic cross-chain UX
Per-pathway configuration burden: send/receive libraries, UlnConfig, peers, and enforced options must be set bilaterally on every lane, and each new chain is N-way work
Executor gas estimation risk: underfunded lzReceive/lzCompose options leave messages verified-but-undelivered; overfunding wastes fees on every message
Ordered delivery head-of-line blocking: one failed nonce halts all higher nonces until governed clear/skip, which itself must sync app-level nonce state
Default-Stack complacency: lazy opt-in to admin defaults silently centralizes verification on the most popular DVNs
use_cases: Omnichain fungible tokens (OFT): burn/mint or lock/unlock transfers preserving one unified supply across EVM, Solana, and Move chains
Omnichain NFTs (ONFT): moving non-fungible assets natively between chains without wrapped copies
Cross-chain governance: casting votes or executing DAO proposals on remote chains from a home-chain ballot
Cross-chain lending and yield aggregation: locking collateral on one chain and opening positions or harvesting yield on another in one attested message
Composed DeFi flows via lzCompose: token arrival triggers follow-on contract calls (swap, stake, deposit) as a separate destination transaction
Cross-chain state reads (lzRead): pulling remote-chain state into local execution with DVN-attested responses
